data.title: Agencia Comercial Spirits says U.S. chip rules may affect AI computing rollout
data.description:
Key points:
  • Agencia Comercial Spirits said that U.S. regulatory requirements on remote access to advanced semiconductors may affect the timing of its AI computing services and customer arrangements.
  • The company said it is reviewing an interim final rule published November 19 by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security.
  • Agencia said its planned data center business will offer colocation and AI computing services. It clarified that it does not sell or resell semiconductor chips, hardware or servers to customers.
  • The company expects to begin AI computing services once its contracted computing capacity is available, subject to regulatory requirements.
  • The company also said that its AI computing and data center operations remain under development and that its historical operating revenue comes from its whisky business.
  • The stock price traded about 1.5% higher on Friday pre-market hours.

data.title: Austria-supervised crypto firms report 20.4B euros in H1 trading volume
data.description:
Crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) supervised by the Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) reported 20.4 billion euros ($22.37 billion) in trading volume for the first half of 2026.

About 74% of user accounts on these platforms were based in other European Economic Area (EEA) countries, particularly Germany and France, the Austrian financial supervisor said in a press release on Friday.

The 20.4 billion euros in the first half of 2026 exceeded the 17 billion euros reported for the full year of 2025, according to the FMA’s annual report.

The FMA said increasing cross-border activity creates a sharp focus on Europe’s crypto supervisory framework and highlights ongoing discussions about giving the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) an enhanced supervisory role over the industry.

In December 2025, the European Commission proposed transfering “direct supervisory competences” for key pieces of market infrastructure, including CASPs, to ESMA. If adopted by EU lawmakers, ESMA’s role in overseeing EU capital markets would resemble the framework of the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

In September 2025, France became the third European country to call for ESMA to take over supervision of major crypto firms, joining Austrian and Italian securities regulators.

data.title: Global diesel market to run into deficit in second quarter of 2027
data.description:
Key points:
  • While Middle East crude exports recover, diesel shipments are still one third of pre-war levels
  • Kpler sees elevated diesel prices through first half of 2027
  • IEA sees improving 2027 diesel outlook but notes risks from Russian refinery attacks, low stocks
  • Europe in 2027 is among the regions in which supply will lag demand by the largest amount, EA says

By Seher Dareen

The global diesel market is set to flip from a small surplus into deficit in the second quarter of 2027 as maintenance will reduce supply already pressured by conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, forecasts show.

That would keep diesel, which powers trucks and farm machinery, an inflationary pressure point into next year even as prices retreat from record highs.

Diesel futures (LGOc1) have fallen 24% this month, in line with crude . However, Middle East gas oil exports remain about a third of pre-Iran war levels, despite a recovery in crude flows, and Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian refineries.

The two regions accounted for over 28% of global diesel exports in 2025, Kpler data shows. Russia's exports have dropped to about 200,000 barrels per day from 800,000 bpd because of the attacks, IEA analyst Tim Gould said.

Russian outages and heavy planned maintenance will keep global refinery runs 1.3 million bpd below trend next year, Goldman Sachs analysts said.

That will limit any rebuild in inventories, which are already low. Gas oil stocks in Europe's ARA hub are down 19% year-on-year, while US distillate stocks are recovering from their lowest since 2003, hit in late October.

"Our latest data shows stocks growing into 2027 but only slightly," said Rystad analyst Janiv Shah.

Europe and Latin America face the largest shortfalls in the first half of 2027, Energy Aspects forecasts show.

A gradual recovery of Middle East refinery runs to pre-conflict levels looks increasingly unlikely by June 2027, said Natalia Losada of EA, adding downside risks to the 2027 balance.

"We expect elevated prices through the first half of 2027 and possibly beyond," said Kpler analyst David Tonyan.

data.title: What is China's 'national team' and can it stop the stock market slide?
data.description:
China's cabinet flagging a bigger role for "national team" investors in its financial markets has sent stocks flying, with benchmarks recording their biggest gains in more than two years and parts of the beaten-down tech sector making record leaps.

Here are some details about the "team", how it moves markets, and whether it can arrest a selloff that has dragged the blue-chip CSI300 index down by about 20% since late June.

WHO IS CHINA'S NATIONAL TEAM?

The nickname is given to a loose collection of state-backed investors and holding firms. There is no agreed official line-up but there is a main player: Central Huijin, the domestic unit of the sovereign wealth fund China Investment Corp.

Others include the China Securities Finance Corp, China Chengtong Holdings Group, China Reform Holdings Corp as well as investment vehicles controlled by China's foreign exchange regulator.

They are tasked with stabilising the market in times of turbulence and their activities are a constant source of speculation. State-owned companies sometimes play a similar support role, buying back their own shares.

HOW MUCH MONEY HAVE THEY GOT?

China Investment Corp disclosed total assets exceeding $1.57 trillion in its 2024 annual report, spread across global stocks, bonds and about 1% in cash.

It is not clear how much of that is available for investing in Chinese equities, though analysts say funding for that can sometimes come from the central bank.

Central Huijin owns stakes in China's biggest banks, brokers and insurers, according to the CIC annual report.

There are no public details of exactly how the team trades. But during times of market stress, participants often issue statements about what they are buying in order to show the market that they are stepping in.

Friday was the first time the State Council, China's cabinet, had used the term "national team" in a press release, state media said. But there were no details about what would change about its role and, notably for investors, no mention of how much money it would put to work stabilising the market.

WHAT DOES THE NATIONAL TEAM DO?

Central Huijin and others describe themselves as long-term investors.

The "national team" entered the market in a big way during the collapse of 2015, buying exchange-traded funds and big stocks, especially financials, according to a 2023 study by UBS strategists. They were buyers, again, during periods of market weakness in 2023 and 2024.

In 2025, when US tariffs rocked equities, Central Huijin said it was a buyer and the central bank said it had supported it in increasing stock fund holdings. Other players announced plans to buy exchange-traded funds tracking the broad market.

Investment bank analysts use flows in and out of these ETFs as a proxy for "national team" activity. This year, they found the team selling through rallies in January and February.

State investors have accelerated buying since fears of an AI slowdown, weak domestic demand and the prolonged real estate downturn started to send Chinese equities into a tailspin in around August, Macquarie analysts said in a note last month.

CAN THEY TURN AROUND THE MARKET?

Investors don't think so. One reason is that they are not big enough to really change the direction of a stock market that in total is worth almost 95 trillion yuan ($14 trillion).

The other is that this is not necessarily their intent.

"We think the importance is the signalling effect," said Winnie Wu, head of Asia equity strategy and co-head of China equity research at BofA Global Research:

"At this point, we think investors will still have the underlying question: Does this change the fundamentals? Does it change the supply-demand dynamics in the tech sector? Does it solve China's bottlenecks in access to compute or semi production capability? It doesn't. It hasn't."

($1 = 6.6543 Chinese yuan renminbi)

data.title: Russian domestic natural gas price may complicate talks with China, analyst says
data.description:
Russia now sells natural gas on the domestic market at higher prices than in the United States, and further increases that outpace inflation could complicate Moscow's negotiations with China over the Power of Siberia 2 pipeline project, an analyst said on Friday.

  • Alexei Gromov, energy director at the Institute for Energy and Finance, told a conference that wholesale gas prices in the Moscow region had reached 8,500 roubles ($103.13) per 1,000 cubic metres, compared with $80 to $95 per 1,000 cubic metres for industrial consumers in the US

  • While Russian gas prices remain well below those in Europe, US consumers now pay less for gas than their Russian counterparts

  • Gromov said rising domestic prices could cast doubt on the economic viability of the proposed Power of Siberia 2 pipeline between Russia and China

  • "By the time this project comes online, if it is launched after 2030, I think gas prices in Russia will already exceed $120-$130 per 1,000 cubic metres. The fundamental question is what pricing formula Russia and China will agree on," he said

  • If the agreed price, including transportation costs, is close to Russian domestic levels, the project would effectively allow Russia to export additional gas at domestic prices, making it an extension of the Russian domestic market, Gromov said

($1 = 82.4221 roubles)

data.title: Bayer to invest up to €500M in Beijing site, its largest pharma investment in China to date
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bayer on Friday announced plans to expand its Pharmaceuticals Product Supply Center in Beijing at a cost of up to €500M, the company’s single largest pharmaceutical investment in China to date.
  • Once complete, the site in the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area will support the production of Bayer’s cardiovascular drugs and future oncology products mainly for Chinese consumers, the company said.
  • The new plant will be built on Bayer’s existing pharmaceutical manufacturing site in Beijing, and it is expected to begin production in 2032, accommodating up to 300 employees, the German conglomerate added. 
  • Since its operations at the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area began in 1997, the company has expanded its pharma site there in 2006 and 2016, making the location its largest packaging facility for prescription drugs globally.

data.title: Altria's pursuit of Imperial Brands could have implications for Anheuser-Busch
data.description:
Imperial Brands formally responded to reports of a potential acquisition offer from Altria . The board said it has not had any discussions with, or received any approach or proposal from, Altria .

The board noted that it is clear in its duty of aiming to maximize shareholder value and will consider any proposal, should one be made. Imperial Brands said it has strong confidence in its strategy and trading.

On Wall Street, Citi analyst Simon Hales said a deal has considerable strategic logic for Altria since it could diversify its cigarette business geographically and add needed scale in next-generation products. While Citi expects no issues funding the transaction, funding the transaction could prompt Altria to lower or exit its roughly $12B stake in Anheuser-Busch InBev . Jefferies analyst Edward Mundy noted that if Anheuser-Busch InBev absorbs the Altria stake, it would be high single-digit earnings accretive.

Shares of Imperial Brands rose 6.6% in London trading on Friday. Altria was down 1.4%, and Anheuser-Busch InBev showed a decline of 2.2%.

data.title: What different election outcomes would mean for Spain's banks
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX up 1 %, as stock markets bounce globally
  • Miners, tech lead gains
  • S&P futures up 1.5%

WHAT DIFFERENT ELECTION OUTCOMES WOULD MEAN FOR SPAIN'S BANKS

Spain holds a snap election this weekend, and Jefferies have a note out looking at what the possible outcomes could mean for the country's banks, big beasts in its stock market.

The conservative People's Party (PP) is ahead of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's Socialists (PSOE) in opinion polls, though these suggest the PP would likely ‌need a coalition with the far-right, anti-immigrant Vox to govern.

But the polls can be wrong, and this is the outcome Jefferies expects for Spanish banks in four scenarios.

1. A comfortable PP + Vox majority, led by a strong PP and with Vox broadly contained.

They think this would see Spanish banks outperform European peers by low to mid single digits as it would offer the cleanest combination of governability, a more business-friendly policy mix, a moderate stance on immigration, and potential upside from revisiting the bank levy.

2. PP + Vox win, but driven by a materially stronger-than-expected Vox.

They think this means a mixed, potentially modestly negative, reaction for banks, as greater parliamentary stability could be offset by a higher political risk premium and uncertainty over the balance of power within government.

3. PP + Vox falling short of a majority

Jefferies expect some underperformance from Spanish banks in this scenario as a higher political and sovereign risk premium translates into a higher cost of equity.

4. A PSOE-led coalition government with key left-wing allies

Here they expect low to mid single digit underperformance versus European peers as the result implies "a more interventionist regulatory backdrop for real estate and reduced optionality around the bank tax."

data.title: BMC gets ready for municipal bond issue, will soon file papers with Sebi: Bhide
data.description:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), the country’s richest civic body, is preparing to launch its maiden municipal bond issue and is in the process of filing papers with market regulator Sebi, a top official said on Friday.

Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide said the civic body is planning to open the proposed issuance to retail investors and institutional participants.

The municipal body is currently planning a general bond issue, but may explore thematic bonds, including green, blue and social bonds, in the future to finance infrastructure projects aligned with its climate action plan, she said.

”We are fully ready for that. We have all the market intermediaries in place, and we are filing our papers with Sebi and we will come up with (the issue),” Bhide said during the panel discussion at Trust Group’s 6th India Debt Capital Market Summit, here.

She refrained from sharing specific details of the bond issue, like issue size or the timeline for when it plans to hit the market. In September, there were media reports saying the body was targeting to raise around Rs 9,500 crore from a bond sale.

Bhide said the civic body expects significant participation from institutional investors while also seeking to provide an opportunity for retail investors to participate in Mumbai’s infrastructure development.

”We expect a lot of institutional investors in that, but at the same time, we want to open it for the retail investors as well. So basically, Mumbaikars can very well participate in the whole growth story of Mumbai,” she said.

The proposed bond issue is part of BMC’s efforts to diversify funding sources as it undertakes a large portfolio of infrastructure projects requiring substantial capital investment.

BMC has an annual budget of nearly ₹80,000 crore, of which around ₹48,000 crore is being spent on infrastructure projects, Bhide said. The civic body has traditionally relied on its own reserves and special funds to finance such projects.

However, she said, the scale of planned infrastructure development and the concentration of expenditure over a relatively short period would require alternative sources of financing.

Apart from the bond market, BMC is looking at institutional finance, public-private partnerships (PPPs) and funding from multilateral agencies.

The civic body is also working on a more robust policy framework to intensify PPP projects across sectors, including healthcare, education and municipal properties.

The civic body’s urban flood mitigation projects and other initiatives aligned with its climate action plan could be among the areas requiring such financing.

BMC has also submitted certain projects under the Centre’s Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) scheme and is in discussions with the central government to link some of its future projects to the initiative.

data.title: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
data.description:
Key points:
  • Zara, H&M, M&S, Celio shift Bangladesh orders, mostly to India
  • Brands divert $254 million in orders as factories shut
  • Bangladesh unrest causes over $400 million in production losses
  • Rising wages, energy shortages erode Bangladesh's cost edge
  • Temporary order shifts risk becoming long-term sourcing moves

By Ruma Paul

Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising costs eroded the country's competitive edge, three factory owners said.

Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, in a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh's economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world's second-largest apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.

The protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings and nearly 40% of its manufacturing jobs.

VIETNAM, CAMBODIA AND INDONESIA ALSO BENEFIT

India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the order diversions, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said.

Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, though the rise was the smallest in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers' demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was "satisfactory" and that he hoped all garment workers would resume work from Saturday.

Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh's labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global apparel industry standards.

The factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of the business.

Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters’ questions, while M&S , H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.

Indian textile shares rallied after the Reuters report, with Gokaldas Exports jumping as much as 11% and Trident gaining about 5%. Other potential beneficiaries, including Welspun Living , KPR Mill and Vardhman Textiles rose around 2% each.

M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, said higher wages, utility and raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers.

"The wage increase has added to costs at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries is intensifying," he said.

Mahmud Hasan Khan, the group's president, declined to name the brands but said temporarily shifting some orders elsewhere helps the industry retain global clients while minimising financial losses.

MORE BUSINESS AT RISK

Factory owners said the bigger concern was that orders already diverted could be followed by the loss of future business as buyers reassessed where to source garments.

Persistent energy shortages, exacerbated by the Middle East crisis, have added to production disruptions and forced some factories to rely on more expensive alternative power sources.

Chowdhury said buyers were increasingly prioritising delivery times over price when choosing suppliers.

"Price becomes secondary when brands are under pressure to meet strict delivery deadlines," he said.

India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead times by as much as 15 days, Chowdhury said.

Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added.

The disruptions have also created production backlogs, with manufacturers around Dhaka losing an estimated 20 to 25 production days. Some are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet delivery commitments.

Khan Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which mainly supplies European brands, said the unrest was already hitting new business.

"Since November 1, most of my buyers have stopped placing orders because of the unrest," Alam said. "They are telling us our orders have been shifted, postponed or cancelled and that they have already found alternative solutions."

Political tensions surrounding former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's possible return to Dhaka from India have added to concerns about further disruption.

Industry leaders said restoring stability and uninterrupted production would be critical to retaining international buyers. Chowdhury warned that orders shifted elsewhere during periods of instability might not return even after conditions improved.

"The challenge is restoring buyers' confidence before temporary shifts become long-term sourcing decisions," he said. "Brands have options. They will not wait for us if instability persists."

data.title: Oil gains lift UAE stocks amid Gulf supply disruption fears
data.description:
By Shamsuddin Mohd

UAE stock markets closed higher on Friday, supported by stronger oil prices as concerns over supply disruptions grew following attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure.

Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery temporarily halted some operations after a projectile struck it on Thursday, killing a Nepalese worker and wounding several others, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said in a statement.

Oil prices, a major driver for Gulf economies, gained on Friday and are on track to snap a three-week losing streak, with Brent crude futures rising 73 cents, or 0.8%, to $97.30 a barrel by 0935 GMT, after hitting their highest since November 9 earlier in the session.

In Dubai, the main share index advanced 1.4%, led by a 2% rise in blue-chip developer Emaar Properties .

Dubai Islamic Bank gained 0.4%, extending recent gains, while Emirates NBD climbed 3.3%.

DIB said on Wednesday that it would acquire smaller rival Emirates Islamic Bank from parent Emirates NBD in an all-share transaction as they seek to create an Islamic lender with roughly $159 billion of assets.

Dubai's benchmark surged 5.6% for the week, marking its biggest weekly gain in nearly 17 months and nearly erasing losses triggered by the recent US-Iran conflict, according to LSEG data.

Abu Dhabi's index added 0.5%, supported by a 0.6% increase in the country's largest lender First Abu Dhabi Bank and a 1.8% lift in Aldar Properties after it said it generated more than 900 million dirhams ($245.06 million) in sales at the launch of its Canopies Sanctuary project on Yas Island.

Abu Dhabi's index climbed 1.8% for the week, according to LSEG data.

"UAE markets advanced on Friday, although caution may persist after US core inflation accelerated and escalating regional tensions continued to disrupt Gulf shipping," said Hani Abuagla, senior market analyst at XTB.

data.title: Why EU leaders are struggling to Le Pen-proof the bloc’s €1.6 trillion budget
data.description:
Key points:
  • Budget talks collapse early, with leaders scrapping planned Friday session
  • Latest proposal sets 2028-2034 EU budget at €1.582 trillion
  • Le Pen vows to cap French EU contributions at €5 billion a year if elected
  • Germany demands all members join a planned 2027 Ukraine loan
  • Single-country veto could force all members to restart negotiations from scratch

By Jan Strupczewski

European Union leaders' talks on the bloc's 2028-2034 budget collapsed on Thursday, with divisions among member states proving deeper than anyone had anticipated. While no breakthrough had been expected, the rifts between the 27 countries were so stark that the gathering was cut short, with the leaders abandoning a second day of talks originally planned for Friday, unwilling to make compromises.

Most of them had hoped to lock in a legally binding deal before the end of the year — and well before France's presidential election in April-May 2027 that could bring far-right leader Marine Le Pen to power. Attention now turns to crunch talks scheduled for December 17-18, where negotiators will have to make up lost ground.

HOW BIG IS THE EU’S BUDGET AND WHERE DOES THE MONEY COME FROM?

The latest proposal, already scaled down from the original in 2025, puts the seven-year budget at €1.582 trillion.

Two-thirds of the budget comes from national contributions based on each country's gross national income, which is why governments fight tooth and nail to keep their net payments as small as possible.

The budget also gets money from:

  • 75% of all customs duties on imports from outside the EU collected by EU countries

  • 0.3% of each country's value-added tax receipts, calculated from a harmonized base so contributions are comparable despite differing VAT rates

  • a levy of €0.80 per kilogram (€800 per ton) of non-recycled plastic packaging waste from each country

  • competition law fines, contributions of non-EU countries to certain EU programmes and taxes on EU staff salaries

To boost revenue and reduce national contributions, EU governments are considering assigning the revenue from the following sources to the EU budget: a digital services tax on large companies, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, non-recycled electronic waste, tobacco products, and the carbon Emissions Trading System.

WHAT HAS LE PEN SAID ABOUT FRENCH CONTRIBUTIONS IF SHE WINS THE PRESIDENCY?

The prospect of a Le Pen presidency is focusing minds in EU countries, since she has vowed to cap French contributions to the EU budget at €5 billion a year. France is the bloc's second-biggest net contributor after Germany, paying between €21 billion and €31 billion a year gross and around €9 billion net. It is unclear whether Le Pen's €5 billion cap refers to gross or net contributions.

Le Pen has also said France would halt financial support for Ukraine against Russia's invasion if she wins, shifting a larger burden onto other EU countries wanting to keep helping Kyiv.

HOW COULD SHE DERAIL THE PROCESS?

Because the EU budget must be agreed unanimously, a single veto can derail the process. If no legally binding deal is reached before Le Pen takes office, she could use that veto, sending all 27 countries back to the drawing board.

Also, the funding agreement, called the "Own Resources Decision," must be ratified by most national parliaments, including France's. If EU governments reach a budget deal before France's April-May elections but it isn't yet ratified there, the deal would not be legally binding and could unravel.

WHAT ARE EU MEMBER STATES HAGGLING OVER?

Size of budget: Net contributors and net beneficiaries are sharply split over the budget's overall size — contributors want it much smaller, while beneficiaries want it to grow.

Rebates: Net contributors also want rebates to further cut what they send to EU coffers, making it harder to fund priorities such as security and defence, competitiveness, climate action, agriculture and support for poorer regions.

How to spend it: Another sticking point is what to spend the money on. Most cash still goes to supporting farmers and fishermen and raising living standards in poorer regions — policies that have dominated the budget for decades. Some countries want to shift funds toward research, innovation and new technologies to bolster the EU's competitiveness against rivals like China and the United States.

HOW IS THE BUDGET APPROVED?

The budget must be unanimously agreed by all 27 EU governments, then negotiated with the European Parliament. Afterward, the "Own Resources Decision" covering all funding sources must be ratified by national parliaments.

HOW IS MONEY FOR UKRAINE LINKED TO THE EU BUDGET?

The EU agreed last year to lend Ukraine €90 billion for 2026-2027. All EU governments except Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic agreed to jointly borrow the money against the EU budget — a move that still required unanimous approval, including from the three reluctant countries.

A new €45 billion loan for 2027 is to be arranged the same way, but this time Germany and others insist all 27 countries must participate — Germany says it won't agree to the 2028-2034 budget otherwise.

The EU has also earmarked €100 billion for Ukraine in its 2028-2034 budget. That is unlikely to be enough: interest alone on Ukraine's existing EU loans, also paid by the EU, will total €55 billion to €65 billion over that period, officials say. Financing Ukraine's loans and interest is a challenge for governments already struggling with heavy public debt and voter displeasure over living costs.

data.title: Linjemontage receives an award decision of approximately SEK 1 billion over three and a half years from Svenska kraftnät
data.description:
INSIDE INFORMATION: Linjemontage i Grästorp AB (publ) ("Linjemontage" or the "Company"), one of Sweden’s leading pure-play EPC providers within power infrastructure, has today received an award decision in a public procurement process from Svenska kraftnät relating to the construction of a new 400 kV power line between Oskarshamn municipality and Nybro municipality (the "Project"). The Project runs over three and a half years and has an estimated contract value of approximately SEK 1 billion. The award for the Project is subject to a statutory standstill period, which means that an agreement may be entered into no earlier than ten days from today.

The project involves approximately 98 kilometres of power line between Ekhyddan in Oskarshamn municipality and Nybro in Nybro municipality, and aims to strengthen the transmission grid, increase capacity and operational reliability, and reduce the risk of power cuts in the region. In recent years, Linjemontage has been awarded several major transmission projects by Svenska kraftnät. Among other things, the company is responsible for the construction of the new 400/220 kV substations in Plenninge and Jälla, outside Uppsala, which form part of Svenska kraftnät’s Uppsala package.

“The expansion and modernisation of the electricity grid is essential for industrial growth and Sweden’s continued electrification. The new transmission line between Ekhyddan and Nybro strengthens electricity transmission in southern Sweden and helps balance supply across the region. This is one of the largest transmission projects we have been awarded to date and, together with our ongoing substation projects in Jälla and Plenninge, demonstrates our ability to deliver large-scale and technically complex high-voltage projects. We thank Svenska kraftnät for the continued confidence in us and look forward to applying our expertise and experience to building a stronger electricity grid.” says Anders Åkerberg, CEO of Linjemontage.

The project is expected to commence at the end of 2026 and is scheduled for completion in June 2030. The works include, amongst other things, excavation and groundworks, foundation construction, the assembly and erection of steel pylons, cable laying, and the commissioning of the new facility.

The award decision regarding the Project is subject to a mandatory ten-day standstill period under the Act on Procurement in the Utilities Sectors (Sw. Lag (2016:1146) om upphandling inom försörjningssektorerna), which means that a contract may be entered into no earlier than after the standstill period has expired. During this period, the decision may be subject to review, and the outcome of the Project therefore cannot be guaranteed. The Company will inform the market of any changes in the Project process in accordance with the (EU) Market Abuse Regulation 596/2014 (MAR).

During the fourth quarter 2026, Linjemontage has also been awarded six new contracts with a total value of approximately SEK 314 million, in addition to those already announced in press releases. That total includes an award decision of approximately SEK 132 million that is currently under standstill period, and will be separately announced when the contract is signed.

This information constitutes inside information as defined in the (EU) Market Abuse Regulation 596/2014 (MAR), which Linjemontage i Grästorp AB (publ) is required to disclose in accordance with MAR. The information was submitted for publication by the contact person listed below, at 2026-11-27 13:11 CET.

Contacts

Thomas Hendel, CFO at Linjemontage

ir@linjemontage.se

About Us

Linjemontage is a Swedish pure-play EPC provider within power infrastructure, enabling the modernisation and expansion of the Nordic electricity grid. The company provides turnkey solutions within substations and transmission and distribution networks, with capabilities across the entire project value chain and specialist high-voltage expertise up to 400 kV. The company currently has approximately 400 employees. Operations are primarily conducted in Sweden and Norway, complemented by a business branch in Croatia and an operation centre in India. Linjemontage was founded in Grästorp in 1993 and the company’s shares have been listed on Nasdaq Stockholm since 2026. For more information, visit www.linjemontage.se

data.title: Chile's jobless rate rises to 10% in quarter through October
data.description:
Chile's unemployment rate hit 10% in the quarter through October, statistics agency INE said on Friday, above the 9.8% expected by economists polled by Reuters.

The Andean country's jobless rate also rose from 9.8% in the previous rolling quarter.
